about.text: Dadiah (Minangkabau) or dadih is a traditional fermented milk popular among people of West Sumatra, Indonesia. It is made by pouring fresh, raw, unheated, buffalo milk into a bamboo tube capped with a banana leaf and allowing it to ferment spontaneously at room temperature for two days.

how.text: Lactic acid bacteria from the raw milk, the bamboo and the banana leaves sour the milk without any added starter. Because every tube starts from a different set of bacteria, the microbes differ from tube to tube even in one village.
